properties.TRAIL_DESC: Gradual, shady paved path that connects Mount Diablo Blvd with the Lafayette Recreation parking area.
Access trail along a flat old ranch road that connects Rancho Laguna Park with Rocky Ridge Trail.
Paved, relatively flat, trail that meanders along the Lafayette Reservoir shoreline. Offers access to the Lafayette Visitor Center, exercise area and docks.

This trail is a short but important link between the City of Orinda and EBMUD's trail system. From the Orinda Connector Trailhead, the trail winds down a steep slope to San Pablo Creek. At the junction, turn right (northeast) and cross San Pablo Creek to continue onto Bear Creek Trail or continue (northwest) on the Orinda Connector Trail past the EBMUD Watershed Headquarters, where the trail becomes Old San Pablo Trail. This leads to the San Pablo Reservoir Boat Launch and beyond.

From the Pereira Trailhead, cross the creek and turn left (west) at the trail junction. The trail passes through open grassland, skirts rolling, grassy hills, and climbs to the top of the Pinole ridgeline. At the crest, the trail connects with the Fernandez Ranch Windmill Trail. From here, continue west to the Franklin Canyon Trail junction, or follow along the Bay Area Ridge Trail, down steep terrain to Alhambra Valley Road below. Bicycles are allowed along the multi-use trail, which consists of fire roads that may be muddy well into spring.

The trail begins at the Old San Pablo Trail, on the north side of the San Pablo Recreation Area. The trail crosses San Pablo Dam Road at a crosswalk and heads uphill into an aromatic eucalyptus forest. Hike steadily uphill to Nimitz Way, then head north to Wildcat Canyon or south into Tilden Regional Park. Bicycles are allowed on the Eagle¿s Nest Trail.

The Skyline Trail begins near the Tilden Steam Trains at the Lomas Cantadas Trailhead and continues off EBMUD land into Sibley Volcanic Regional Preserve. The trail has beautiful ridgeline views and a wide assortment of native flora in the spring. The Skyline Trail is also accessible from the Skyline Gardens Trailhead on Grizzly Peak Blvd.

The trail is accessible from Rocky Ridge Trail, approximately 2.3 miles from the Rancho Laguna Trailhead. The trail passes through a range of ecosystems, including live oak woodlands, riparian woodlands along Buckhorn Creek, coastal scrub and annual grasslands. The trail follows a rolling ridgeline before reconnecting with Rocky Ridge Trail. Dogs are allowed.
This steep, oak shaded trail connects the east side of the main parking lot to the Rim trail.

From Valle Vista Staging Area, follow the unpaved fire road to the right (west), leading to a foot trail that descends into a redwood forest. After crossing Indian Creek, the trail emerges onto Canyon Road. It picks up again across Pinehurst Road, crosses San Leandro Creek, and winds steadily upslope to East Ridge Trail in Redwood Regional Park.
Provides access from the Pinole Valley Multi-use Trail to the Franklin Ridge Trail in Fernandez Ranch.
Steep ascent along a service road that connects the southern portion of the Bear Creek trail with the Oursan Trail at the top of the dam.

A challenging, strenuous trail that connects the east side of the Lakeside Nature Trail to the Rim Trail.  The Big Oak Trail is a graded dirt fire road that passes through one of Lafayette Reservoirs dense oak woodlands.

A graded dirt fire road that connects the Rim and Canyon trails through grass and brush land.  The Rheem and Rim trail intersection offers broad views of the backcountry canyon area of Lafayette Reservoir.
Short path that connects Skyline Trail with Grizzly Peak Blvd. Access the trail through an opening in the fence just north of the bar gate.
Gradual downhill descent from the Overlook parking lot to the Bear Creek trail. Dogs are permitted on the southern portion of the connector to access the Oursan trail.
Gradual climb along a fire road that connects the Pinole Valley Multi-use Trail with EBRPD¿s Sobrante Ridge Trail.

From Chabot Staging Area, follow Ramage Peak Trail (0.84 miles) to Dinosaur Trail, continue to EBRPD Chabot-to-Garin Trail (2.3 miles). The trail provides some challenging climbs and offers spectacular views that make the effort worthwhile. When you reach Dinosaur Peak, you will see the stegosaurus-back rock outcroppings that inspired the trail name.
From the Hampton Trailhead, hike south along a shady hillside to connect with Oursan Trail. Dogs are allowed.

From the Pereira Trailhead, cross the creek and turn right at the junction. The narrow gauge trail continues up a steep hill through grasslands and coyote brush scrub to Pinole Peak. The trail has nice views of the Pinole Valley and the Bay. It continues along the Pinole Valley Multi-Use Trail along the Bay Area Ridge Trail alignment.

This trail begins along Rocky Ridge Trail, approximately 3.5 miles from the Rancho Laguna Trailhead. However, more direct access is available via Las Trampas Regional Wilderness. This trail of unpaved fire roads offers a close-up view of Rocky Ridge and splendid views of the lands beyond. The trail is steep in multiple areas.

This trail starts just beyond the bridge that crosses Moraga Creek on Rocky Ridge Trail, approximately 0.4 miles from Valle Vista Staging Area. The trail branches left (east), parallel to Rimer Creek through great birding habitat. It climbs uphill to reconnect with Rocky Ridge Trail. Turn right (west) on Rocky Ridge Trail to loop back to Valle Vista Staging Area, passing horse stables along the way.
Gradual descent to Kennedy Grove from the San Pablo Dam.

The trail takes a leisurely route along the west side of the San Pablo Reservoir. The trail between the San Pablo Boat Launch and the San Pablo Dam is wide gauge and paved or gravel fire road. This was once the main road through the San Pablo Valley before construction of the current San Pablo Dam Road. Biking is allowed on the paved and gravel portions of the old road.

This is a long, dog-friendly trail that follows unpaved fire roads. Head south from the Briones Overlook Staging Area and turn right (northwest) across the Briones Reservoir Dam. The trail follows the crest of Sobrante Ridge to the north side of the reservoir. After the Hampton Trail intersection, the trail continues along the reservoir for another 5.5 miles to the Bear Creek Staging Area. If you are traveling without a dog, you can make a long loop (roughly 13 miles) by continuing onto Bear Creek Trail (no dogs allowed), which circles back to the Briones Overlook Staging Area.

This is a fairly strenuous, dog-friendly hike through scenic countryside. The trail begins at Valle Vista Staging Area and ends at Las Trampas Regional Wilderness on Rocky Ridge. The trail is also accessible from Rancho Laguna Trailhead. Choose from a number of loops to extend the length of your adventure.

The trail begins at Inspiration Point in Tilden Regional Park and drops down the broad shoulders of San Pablo Ridge through grassy pastures to the San Pablo Reservoir below. Use the pedestrian crosswalk at San Pablo Dam Road to connect with Old San Pablo Trail.
This is a winding, easy, paved trail that encircles the reservoir. The popular paved trail is open to bicyclists during limited hours.
A steady but gentle climb from the Lakeside Nature, through oak savanna, to the Rim Trail.  The graded dirt fire road offers sweeping views of Lafayette Reservoir and surrounding hills.

This trail traverses the southeast slopes of the Briones Reservoir. It is moderately steep in a few sections, mostly forested, and botanically fascinating. At the Bear Creek Staging Area, head through the south gate and cross the creek to get on the trail. Hike past the Briones Overlook Staging Area to continue downhill along the Briones Dam spillway to the Orinda Connector Trail.

This unpaved fire road traverses the ridge tops surrounding the Lafayette Reservoir. Starting at the fish cleaning station near the west pines picnic area, the trail leads through brushland and oak forests overlooking the reservoir. Well-graded fire roads connect the Rim trail to the Lakeside Nature Trail in several locations.

This spectacular route passes through some of the most remote watershed lands in the East Bay. From Chabot Staging Area, cross the service road and follow the path above the Christmas tree farm. The trail zigzags along fire roads and narrow gauge trails through ranch lands, old homesteads and a number of different habitats. The trail climbs up to Ramage Peak and connects to Rocky Ridge Loop.

This trail provides access to the East Bay Skyline National Recreation Trail from the City of Orinda. The trail is a challenging climb with several steep sections that lead to spectacular ridgetop views. The trail ends at Skyline Trail, just below Grizzly Peak Boulevard near Tilden Steam Train.

A moderate climb from the Lakeside Nature Trail to the west side of the Rim Trail.  The Canyon Trail is a graded dirt fire road that passes through grass and brush land.  Hikers often combine the Canyon and Rheem trail to bypass the southern, steepest section of the Rim Trail.

From the Lakeside Nature Trail, the Campolindo Trail is a steady uphill climb to the Rim Trail on a graded dirt fire road.  The Campolindo Trail provides a scenic mixture of annual grass and oak woodlands.

This trail is a short, dog-friendly loop, accessible from Valle Vista Staging Area. The trail passes through pasture and scrub habitat and provides a view of the north shore of the Upper San Leandro Reservoir.

The trail is accessible from Rocky Ridge Trail, 0.85 mile from Valle Vista Staging Area. The trail winds through oak forests and skirts Upper San Leandro Reservoir. Loop back to Valle Vista Staging Area by following the Rocky Ridge Trail up and down a moderately steep hill. Dogs are allowed.

The trail takes a leisurely route along the west side of the San Pablo Reservoir. The trail section between Orinda Watershed Headquarters and the San Pablo Boat Launch is narrow gauge and mostly shaded by a Monterey pine grove. No bicycles are allowed on the narrow portion of the trail.
Steep trail that connects the Rim trail to the intersection Moraga Road and Via Granada in Lafayette.
